category: Advanced Training, Adaptation, and Model Surgery
definition: Training on convex combinations of input pairs and their labels (Mixup), or on images with patches swapped between examples (CutMix).
details: Training on convex combinations of input pairs and their labels (Mixup), or on images with patches swapped between examples (CutMix). Vision-era regularizers whose spirit survives in modern augmentation stacks, including SpecAugment-adjacent recipes in speech.

explainer.lead: Mixup and CutMix are augmentation methods that train on convex combinations of input pairs and labels, or on images with patches swapped between examples. They matter as regularizers that improve generalization and whose spirit survives in modern augmentation stacks.

tiers.eli5: Show the model blended or patch-swapped pictures with blended answers, so it learns to be less rigid about any single example.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply them to reduce overfitting in vision training; a pitfall is that overly aggressive mixing can blur labels and hurt accuracy on fine-grained tasks.
tiers.paperLevel: Mixup trains on convex combinations of input pairs and their labels; CutMix swaps patches between images; both are vision-era regularizers echoed in modern augmentation recipes including SpecAugment-adjacent speech methods.

explainer.example: Blending two images and their one-hot labels 70/30 creates a training example whose target reflects both classes.
